title: PROFESSIONALISM AND ENGINEERING ETHICS
description: Introduces professionalism and engineering ethics through presentation of ethical theory, professional engineering responsibility, codes of ethics, conflicts of obligation, conflicts of interest, risk and safety, and loyalty and dissent. Explores the social and political dimensions of engineering and “macroethical” topics such as sustainability and bioethics.
registration_restrictions:
Prerequisites: CBEE 212, 212H or 280.
A minimum grade of C is required in CBEE 212, CBEE 212H and CBEE 280.

Enrollment limited to students in the College of Engineering college.
